source_review.notes: Checked current or explicitly versioned official Apache Iceberg specification, partitioning, evolution, Spark DDL/write/query, and API documentation; Trino Iceberg connector and Apache Spark data-source documentation; Delta Lake liquid-clustering documentation; and Apache Hudi, Paimon, and Hive layout documentation. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Iceberg-specific evolution semantics are attributed, while contrasting layout mechanisms are not presented as equivalent protocols.

evidence: Reviewed logical predicate q, identified specs sigma_k, transform tuples tau_k, source and partition-field identities, inclusive projections pi_k, residuals, file cohorts, candidate sets, and cohort bytes/files/rows.
Checked per-spec subset soundness, candidate union, transform function g_k, and cohort-scoped ratios.
Checked that source values, transformed partition values, path strings, tuple positions, display names, field IDs, and spec IDs remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Partition counts and labels from different transform domains are never added or compared as if they represented one shared domain.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced two specs planned, old-day.parquet retained by day projection, new-10.parquet retained by hour projection, sorted union of both candidates, and residual_required=yes.
Recomputed cohort retention as 200/1000=20% and 6/300=2%.
Recomputed aggregate retention as 206/1300 approximately 15.85%, while preserving the warning that file counts omit bytes and latency.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No universal partition count, granularity, bucket count, convergence percentage, file size, pruning ratio, or migration duration is prescribed.

evidence: Verified per-spec inclusive projection implies every matching file belongs to its cohort candidate set and therefore to the union across active specs.
Verified old-file stability from immutable file/manifest metadata and retained exact spec identity after default-spec evolution.
Verified convergence equivalence and overwrite auditing require row/deletion semantics and logical predicates, not copied tuples, path lists, or equal counts.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Projection prunes partitions conservatively; the original or proven-equivalent residual supplies exact row semantics.

evidence: Reviewed null input, negative truncation, Unicode, binary, decimals, epoch/timezone and daylight-saving boundaries, range endpoints, conjunction, disjunction, and unsafe negation.
Reviewed unpartitioned-to-partitioned, month/day/hour, bucket-count, truncate-width, add/drop/rename/reorder, unknown transforms, legacy positional fields, and metadata-table nulls.
Reviewed stale writers, old-spec appends, dynamic overwrite, predicate delete, compaction, concurrent spec change, path deletion, mixed delete files, rollback, and partial convergence.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Unknown pruning semantics retain affected files or explicitly fail according to protocol; writers never invent unknown transform results.

evidence: Traced source-field ID, partition-field ID, transform and parameters, result type, name, spec ID, manifest, file tuple, table default, query projection, candidate, and residual.
Checked each file is interpreted under exactly its writer spec and every current logical predicate is independently projected for each active cohort.
Checked atomic default-spec publication, staged-writer validation, overwrite scope, rewrite recomputation, delete preservation, retained old specs, and rollback reachability.
invariant_checking.notes: Changing the default controls future layout; it neither relabels historical tuples nor completes physical convergence.

evidence: Reviewed mixed-spec pruning, old-file stability, convergence equivalence, overwrite audit, and deployment proof obligations.
Checked counterexamples for current-spec-only planning, cross-count bucket equality, negated inclusive projection, dynamic overwrite after evolution, and tuple-copying compaction.
Checked transform fixtures and conservative full-scan comparisons cover hash, truncation, time boundaries, nulls, unknown transforms, mixed specs, cached metadata, and concurrent changes.
proof_review.notes: The proof scope requires correct format transforms, stable identity, immutable metadata, inclusive file statistics, and residual evaluation.

evidence: Audited partition spec, partition field, source field, transform, hidden partitioning, evolution, cohort, projection, candidate, and residual terminology.
Confirmed physical partition, directory path, metadata-table field, logical predicate, overwrite scope, and snapshot reachability are distinguished.
Confirmed metadata-only evolution, natural convergence, targeted rewrite, immediate convergence, and shadow migration are separate actions.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Product-specific unknown-transform, legacy-ID, and overwrite behavior is labeled rather than generalized to every table format.

evidence: Reviewed files, rows, bytes, manifests, partitions, age, skew, small files, projected predicates, candidates, residuals, metadata/data bytes, planning/scan time, cache, stale writers, and overwrite scope by spec.
Confirmed query and maintenance evidence is segmented by snapshot, spec ID, transform, source field, engine/version, writer, time range, and warm/cold state where relevant.
Confirmed aggregate pruning, bucket count, one canary file, successful DDL, or equal row count is not mislabeled as correctness or fleet-value proof.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Convergence decisions require measured workload benefit against I/O, compute, conflict, retention, and operational risk.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed typed specs and transforms, hidden partitioning, inclusive projection, residuals, mixed-spec union, evolution operations, temporal and bucket changes, overwrite semantics, concurrent writers, convergence, observability, and verification.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable spec inventories, field IDs, transform vectors, client capability checks, DDL publication, stale-writer policy, explicit predicate overwrites, per-cohort metrics, convergence selection, keyed reconciliation, delete preservation, canaries, fault tests, retention, and rollback. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from spec identity through projection and mixed-layout planning to operations and convergence. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover month/day, bucket changes, new fields, rename, dynamic overwrite, stale writers, rewrite, negation, misleading aggregate pruning, executable union, hour queries, bucket equality, overwrite safety, validation, and cohort arithmetic.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Iceberg/Trino/Spark/Delta Lake/Hudi/Paimon/Hive maintainer, query-engine or table-format implementer, database/distributed-systems/storage/platform/streaming/security specialist, data owner, production operator, affected consumer, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
